messages.subject_clean: Making a reactive variable wait for observe to finish?
messages.body_plain:
Hmmm, it should work. Reactives don't fire directly, they are invalidated by the button click (if they have a dependency) but that doesn't make them execute. It's an observer or output that has also been invalidated, that has to cause it to execute.

You can use the reactlog tool to see exactly what's causing that code to run:
Restart R session
options(shiny.reactlog=TRUE)
shiny::runApp()
Press the button or whatever
Press Ctrl+F3 in the browser (or Cmd+F3 on Mac)
Then use left/right arrow keys to see exactly what code is being triggered by what.

messages.body_plain:
Ok thanks for the hint! That is a cool tool. I tracked down the problem.

After the button is pushed these events are what I can see in the log:
1) the observe (3) is invalidated.
2) the reactive is invalidated (1)
3) the renderDataTable (2) is in turn invalidated
4) The observer (3) starts running
5) the "isolate" from inside the observer part appears
6) then it shows the reactive (1) running while the observe is still running
7) the reactive (1) finishes running
8) the observe (3) finishes running
9) then the renderDataTable (2) starts running

So I think I understand what happens. The observe part uses the reactive that was also invalidated (since both depend on the button click). So the reactive re-executes because the observe needs it. But only after that is the database modified. So when the renderDataTable uses the reactive it is getting the data from before the database operations.

I managed to create the solution I had tried to do before. Before I tried to assign a reactive inside the "isolate" of the "observe". But the log shows that this new reactive is never invalidated. Instead if I create a reactiveValues outside the observe and then assigns a value from inside the "isolate" of the "observe" it works and I can have the original reactive dependent on this value instead.

Thanks again for your patience. I guess the problem was that I neglected to state that the observe needed to use the original reactive...

run_as shiny;

  location / {

    # Host the directory of Shiny Apps stored in this directory
    site_dir /srv/shiny-server;

    # Log all Shiny output to files in this directory

messages.subject_clean: Installing Shiny Server on Debian 7 (Wheezy)
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I've been attempting to install Shiny Server on my Debian 7 server, but have run into a few problems. Unfortunately reading the documentation didn't produce solutions, or perhaps my reading was not thorough enough. Please berate me if the latter is the case.

Initially I just tried to install the Ubuntu deb file. I found a webpage outlining the process someone had used successfully with Deb 6.

http://www.thecoatlessprofessor.com/programming/r/installing-the-open-source-shiny-server-on-dreamhost-vps-debian

Unfortunately, it seem like an older version of Shiny Server (1.0.0) as used in that post may work, but the newest package I downloaded (1.2.0) no longer does. The install seemed to go fine, but when launching shiny-server I receive the following errors:

/opt/shiny-server/ext/node/bin/shiny-server: /lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libc.so.6: version `GLIBC_2.15' not found (required by /opt/shiny-server/ext/node/bin/shiny-server)
/opt/shiny-server/ext/node/bin/shiny-server: /lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libc.so.6: version `GLIBC_2.14' not found (required by /opt/shiny-server/ext/node/bin/shiny-server)

Deb 7 only has GLIBC_2.13 equivalent. I could install a compatible lib.so.6 from the Experimental repositories, but am extremely reluctant to do so as this has the potential to break everything and reduce me to a snivelling wreck (or at least sigh, swear a lot and start to rebuild the entire server).

My first question is whether it would be possible, or even sensible, to install an old 1.0.0 deb package? Is the upgrade path to 1.2.0 straightforward from an existing installation?

I next tried to build from sources. After messing about with a newer version of cmake from wheezy-backports, I made good progress. However, during the make step I am stopped at the node configuration step with the following errors:

[ 11%] Built target shiny-server
[ 22%] Performing configure step for 'node'
/home/phillc/downloads/shiny-server/external/node/node-v0.10.21/configure
make[2]: *** [external/node/node-prefix/src/node-stamp/node-configure] Error 1
make[1]: *** [external/node/CMakeFiles/node.dir/all] Error 2
make: *** [all] Error 2

While I am comfortable enough building from source, I'm not knowledgeable enough to troubleshoot quite vague make errors such as the one above. I know it's a problem with node configuration, but I have no idea what that configuration error could be.

Any thoughts, hints and suggestions much appreciated.

Phill

messages.body_plain:
Hello everyone,

I developed a shiny app, for testing (alpha versions) it get's deployed to shiny sever. Before shiny server was released, it got tested by just running a R instance. And here is the trouble I am running in.
When the app is running via a R instance, everything is just fine, all data in RAM, shiny is super responsible and answers the first call (via the browser) fast. But when deployed to the shiny server, all data get's first loaded when a client is calling the app (via browser). This results in a) slow responsibility for the user (at the initial call) b) my data is growing and it seems shiny can't handle it (maybe there is timeout via HTTP) and doesn't start (or just when feeling lucky).
I got my in .RData objects, I load from the filesystem, via load() command in the global file. The files are compressed and ~5GB each. So, is there a way to permanently keep them in memory, for every user instance? So the user doesn't have to wait long or it's timing out. I really need to solve this :/
If the app is running, the performance is perfectly fine, just got that startup issue. And my machine isn't running out of memory.

I am running:
- R version 3.1.0
- shiny_0.10.0
- CentOS 6

With best regards,

Mario

On Wednesday, June 4, 2014 12:46:37 PM UTC-5, Yihui Xie wrote:
>
> Hi all,
>
> We’re hoping to submit Shiny 0.10.0 to CRAN shortly, and would love your feedback on some of the new features that we’ve added since 0.9.1. Please help us by installing and testing the latest version from GitHub (the version number is still 0.9.1.x there but will eventually become 0.10.0 on CRAN):
> if (!require('devtools')) install.packages('devtools')
> devtools::install_github('rstudio/shiny')
> Shiny Docs
>
> Many of you are familiar with knitr <http://yihui.name/knitr/> and R Markdown <http://rmarkdown.rstudio.com>, excellent tools for creating documents that combine R code and output with your writing.
>
> With Shiny 0.10 and R Markdown v2, you can easily embed Shiny inputs and outputs, and even entire Shiny applications, right into your R Markdown documents! You can now create documents that allow your readers to change the assumptions underlying your analysis and see the results immediately. R Markdown documents with Shiny apps or widgets embedded are called Shiny Docs.
>
> Shiny Docs combine the expressiveness of R Markdown with the interactivity of Shiny. These documents can be run locally on the desktop or be deployed to ShinyApps <http://shinyapps.io> or Shiny Server <http://www.rstudio.com/products/shiny/shiny-server/> v1.2.
>
> To start writing Shiny Docs, just install the current preview release <http://www.rstudio.com/products/rstudio/download/preview/> of RStudio (v0.98.891) as it includes not only updated versions of the various packages required to run Shiny Docs (including Shiny 0.10) but also tools for previewing and iterative development.
>
> Learn more about Shiny Docs here <http://rmarkdown.rstudio.com/authoring_shiny.html>.
> Server-side processing for selectize input
>
> The client-side selectize input (introduced in shiny 0.9.0) relies solely on JavaScript to process searching on typing. The server-side selectize input uses R to process searching, and R will return the filtered data to selectize. To use the server version, you need to create a selectize instance in the UI, and update it to the server version:
> # in ui.R
> selectizeInput('foo', choices = NULL, ...)
>
> # in server.R
> shinyServer(function(input, output, session) {
>   updateSelectizeInput(session, 'foo', choices = data, server = TRUE)
> })
>
> The server-side processing is particularly useful when the number of choices is very large. For example, when there are 100,000 choices for the selectize input, it will be slow to write and load all of them at once on a page. With the new server-side selectize features, you can start from an empty selectize input, and only fetch the choices that the user searches for, which can be much faster. See this article <http://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/selectize.html> for more information and examples.
> New layout functions
>
> Three new functions, flowLayout(), splitLayout(), and inputPanel(), were added for putting UI elements side by side.
> flowPanel() lays out its children in a left-to-right, top-to-bottom arrangement.
> splitLayout() evenly divides its horizontal space among its children (or unevenly divides if cellWidths argument is provided).
> inputPanel() is like flowPanel(), but with a light grey background, and is intended for encapsulating small input controls wherever vertical space is at a premium.
>
> A new argument inline (TRUE/FALSE) was also added to checkboxGroupInput() and radioButtons() to arrange check boxes and radio buttons horizontally.
> Custom validation error messages
>
> Sometimes you do not want your render functions in server.R to proceed unless certain input conditions are satisfied, e.g. the action button has been clicked, or a select input value has been chosen. In these cases, you may want to either stop the render function quietly, or with a custom message. In shiny 0.10.0, we introduced the functions validate() and need() to specify the validation conditions. See this article <http://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/validation.html> for details and examples.
>
> There have also been a few smaller tweaks and bug fixes. For the full list, you can take a look at the NEWS <https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/blob/master/NEWS> file. Please let us know if you have any comments or questions.
>
> Thanks for your support – we look forward to hearing from you!

messages.subject: Working dir of shiny app when run R rmarkdown document, where shiny is embeded into by `shinyAppDir`
messages.subject_clean: Working dir of shiny app when run R rmarkdown document, where shiny is embeded into by `shinyAppDir`
messages.body_plain:
Hi there,

In shiny apps, the working directory is automatically set to the root directory of the app. And for R markdown, when rendering (also running a shiny doc), the working directory is set to the one which contains the Rmd files.

When I embed a shiny app to a markdown document by shinyAppDir, problems arise: the working directory is set according to the Rmd logic for both R chunks and for shiny app, path I used in shiny apps to import local data need to be changed. In this case I cannot use one app as stand alone as well as embedded one. I can write some code to work around but it becomes complex.

In short, working directory is `APP_ROOT` for shiny apps, but when run as an embedded app in a R markdown, the working directory is different, which is not convenient.

Besides that, I’m considering:

how about store some metadata of shiny.app <http://shiny.app> class? For example the app name.

I prefer to embed shiny apps into a R markdown document, instead of writing text within shiny apps. In this circumstance, the first problem is the working directory I mention earlier. The next one is, when writing a report, we are usually using the same data set and basic logic, we explore different aspects of a single task. So if I write something and embed a shiny and then write something, I have to embed another shiny app. But the long report may be depend on the same dataset and process. What about one server, many ui.R? It seems that design is now bind to server, but isn’t it the right way to bind design to logic but isolate from server?
​

messages.subject: Re: dynamic tabset panels
messages.subject_clean: dynamic tabset panels
messages.body_plain:
Ok, I figured out a way to produce dynamic tabset panels, it's a bit ugly and would like to have your comments on wether i am denaturing Shiny or not. The simplest way I found was to use a series of call() to build the functions to render the tabset using an lapply() dependent on the reactive value input$samples. The list of calls returned is then evaluated by a do.call() with the function tablsetPanel()

It goes like this

output$plotUI <- renderUI({
    ## Dynamically render tabset based on the user selected samples
    do.call(tabsetPanel,
            ## Create a set of tabPanel functions dependent on input$samples
            lapply(input$samples,function(s){
                ## Populate the tabPanel with a dataTableOutput layout, with ID specific to the sample.
                ## Can also accommodate additional layout parts by adding additional call() to call("tabPanel")
                call("tabPanel",s,call('dataTableOutput',paste0("table_",s)))
            })
            )
})

Then, the panels can be populated with data using a simple loop structure like this

lapply(input$samples, function(s){
    ## Add a DataTable of gene selected in the heatmap
    output[[paste0('table_',s)]] <- renderDataTable(values[[s]],options=list(iDisplayLength=10))
    return(s)
})

Obviously, one needs a bit of extra logic to make sure that there is at least one selected samples, etc... Also this structure can be made more complex by adding extra call() arguments to the call("tabPanel") to add additional UI feature to the different tabs (like text, download button, etc...)

I have an almost finished example with quite complex logics on gitub: heatmap-app <https://github.com/mblanche/heatmap-app>

Let me know what you think, whether this is an ugly hack or not. I could see that the do.call()/call() structure could be made as a dynamic function taking variable arguments that would hide the ugliness of the structure...

thanks

Marco

messages.subject: Re: Draw a line with intercept and slope on a ggvis plot
messages.subject_clean: Draw a line with intercept and slope on a ggvis plot
messages.body_plain:
Hi ggvis takes a dataframe as input so maybe something like the following would work:

library(ggvis)

x_min <- 2
x_max <- 5

m <- -1
b <- 2

x <- c(x_min, x_max)
y <- m*x + b

df <- data.frame(x = x, y = y)

df %>% ggvis(x = ~x, y = ~y) %>% layer_lines()

Another approach is to use layer_model_predictions:

df %>% ggvis(x = ~x, y = ~y) %>% layer_model_predictions(model = "lm", formula = y ~ x)

Also, there is an active google group on ggvis: https://groups.google.com/forum/#!forum/ggvis

Hope this helps,

Ian

messages.body_plain:
Eilidh,

I just setup an Apache configuration that is working with Shiny Server. There might be other ways to handle this, but I am not very familiar with Apache. See if this option works for you.

- Edit Apache default configuration and setup a proxy that points to port 3838 (this is the port that Shiny Server is listening on)

sudo vi /etc/apache2/sites-available/default

<VirtualHost *:80>
        ServerAdmin webmaster@localhost

        ProxyPass / http://localhost:3838/
        ProxyPassReverse / http://localhost:3838/
        ProxyPreserveHost On

        Alias /shiny/ "/srv/shiny-server/"
        <Directory "/srv/shiny-server/">
               Options Indexes FollowSymLinks Includes ExecCGI
               Order allow,deny
               Allow from all
       </Directory>

- Restart Apache:

sudo /etc/init.d/apache2 restart

- With this setting, I can access the Shiny Server landing page as http://<hostname>
- I have other applications under /srv/shiny-server. For example: /srv/shiny-server/01_hello
I can access those as http://<hostname>/01_hello or such.

You can change the configuration to the way you want to handle the URLs.

Let me know how it goes, and if you still have problem with this.

Fereshteh

messages.body_plain:
Eilidh,

About the configuration that I suggested, that was just a basic setup to show how you can setup a proxy to listen on port 3838.

The configuration that you need to serve applications at http://internalserver/shiny requires a change like this in your Apache configuration:
(Again, I am not an Apache expert, and you have to consider your server's current setup with any changes you want to make.)

        ProxyPass /shiny/ http://localhost:3838/

        ProxyPassReverse /shiny/ http://localhost:3838/shiny http://localhost:3838/
        ProxyPreserveHost On
        RedirectMatch permanent ^/shiny$ /shiny/

However, we realized (As Jan has also mentioned in an earlier post) that this configuration is not working with the latest version of Shiny Server (v1.2.0.359). We are looking into the issue, and possible workaround for it.

Thanks,
Fereshteh

messages.subject_clean: observe in a for loop
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

Below are a ui.R and server.R. The app takes a list of ids in 'vars'. It creates a dynamic ui of 1 slider for each id in vars. It also creates a reactive observer for each id in vars. However, it does not work like I expect. The three sliders get created just fine. When I move the 1st two sliders, nothing happens in response. When I move the 3rd slider (foo3), it's corresponding observer not only executes, but runs 3 times. Below is example output.

Why aren't the 1st two iterations of the observer loop working? Why does the 3rd observer get called 3 times when the last slider is changed?

ui.R:
library(shiny)
shinyUI(
  uiOutput('gui')
)

server.R:
library(shiny)
shinyServer(function(input, output, session) {
  vars = c('foo1','foo2','foo3')

  for (v in vars){ observe({ print(paste0(v,': ',input[[v]])) }) }

  output$gui <- renderUI({
    fluidPage(
      mapply(sliderInput,vars,vars,MoreArgs=list(min=0,max=10,value=5,step=0.1),SIMPLIFY=FALSE)
    )
  })
})

Output:
Listening on http://127.0.0.1:3048
[1] "foo3: "
[1] "foo3: "
[1] "foo3: "
[1] "foo3: 5"
[1] "foo3: 5"
[1] "foo3: 5"
[1] "foo3: 3.6"
[1] "foo3: 3.6"
[1] "foo3: 3.6"

Helle everybody

I want to colour pologyons i'm displaying on a leaflet map with shiny, using calculated datas.
I don't really understand the option in the leaflet function addPolygon and how can use it to render my polygons.

It's rendering me all the polygon with default color

           My ploygon is named poly

           #Variable to represent : var_deb
               var_deb <- as.vector(poly[,5])

            # Number of classes
               nbclass <- 11

             # Intervals
               distr <- c(-500,-250,-100,-75,-50,-25,-5,0,5,25,50,75,100,250,500)

              # Colors
               colours <- brewer.pal(nbclass, "RdBu")
               colMap <- colours[(findInterval(var_deb, distr, all.inside = TRUE))]

              #Option to pass to addPolygon
              opts=list(fillColor=colMap[1])
                                  for (i in 2:length(colMap))
                                    {
                                    opt=NA
                                    opt=list(fillColor=colMap[i])
                                    opts=c(opts,opt)
                                    }
               map$addPolygon(lat=poly[,2],lng=poly[,1],layerId=poly[,3],options=opts)

Does someone has an idea ?

Thks

Fabien

messages.subject: Re: required_group not working in ldap
messages.subject_clean: required_group not working in ldap
messages.body_plain:
Evan,

The forbidden error usually means that your authentication has been successful, but user does not have permission to view the application. For this, you need specify which users have permission to view the application. The "required_user" directive in shiny-server.conf file is used for this purpose, either for the Admin Dashboard, or any Shiny applications.

An example of shiny-server.conf that requires authentication for certain Shiny applications is in this location in your installation:

/opt/shiny-server/config/auth.config

Let us know if you are still having problem with this. And you can send us your shiny-server.conf file.

messages.body_plain:
Evan,

Very sorry, I missed that line about required_group.

So we need to troubleshoot your setup.
First, please set TRACE logging for your Shiny Server. This gives details about how Shiny Server is trying to access users in LDAP.

Add the following line in your /etc/init/shiny-server.conf file:  (this is for Ubuntu, and CentOS 6. What distribution are you using?)

env SHINY_LOG_LEVEL=TRACE

And then stop and start shiny server. Now try to login and watch /var/log/shiny-server.log file. You should a few lines related to LDAP authentication. This can help you see what filter is being used, and why the user is not found.

Potentioal problems:
1) In your conf file you have:   group_search_base ou=breweries;
Have you tried using ou=Groups?

2) The other thing (which might be just a typo in your posting), you mentioned: "I have a groupOfUniqueNames called pay"
Is it "pay" or "paid"?

Besides the above that I could see as potential problems, I can give you a concrete example (my own setup) that works, and may be that helps you figure out problem with your setup. (and may be it ends up being a Shiny Server problem).

I have the following in my shiny-server.conf file:

auth_ldap ldap://ssp-openldap/dc=ssp-openldap {
  group_filter "memberUid={username}";
  group_search_base ou=Groups;
}

and: required_group managers;

My LDAP has a group cn=managers, which has memberUid=kim.

When I login as user "kim", this is what the log file shows:

[2014-07-11 07:54:40.907] [TRACE] shiny-server - Attempting to bind LDAP user 'uid=kim,ou=People,dc=ssp-openldap'
[2014-07-11 07:54:40.911] [TRACE] shiny-server - Using user DN: uid=kim,ou=People,dc=ssp-openldap
[2014-07-11 07:54:40.913] [TRACE] shiny-server - Retrieving groups for user 'uid=kim,ou=People,dc=ssp-openldap' using filter: '(memberUid=kim)' in 'ou=Groups,dc=ssp-openldap'
[2014-07-11 07:54:40.925] [TRACE] shiny-server - Discovered groups: kim,managers
[2014-07-11 07:54:40.927] [TRACE] shiny-server - Retrieving groups for user 'uid=kim,ou=People,dc=ssp-openldap' using filter: '(memberUid=kim)' in 'ou=Groups,dc=ssp-openldap'

As you can see it uses filter 'memberUid=kim'  (this is the group_filter in my shiny-server.conf file).
in 'ou=Groups' (this is group_search_base in my shiny-server.conf file)

Hope this helps. Let us know otherwise.

Best,
Fereshteh

messages.subject: multiple action buttons with the same inputID -- but only one works
messages.subject_clean: multiple action buttons with the same inputID -- but only one works
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

the buttons are based on the id of the underlying html element on the page i.e the fysical button. Two important concepts of all elements are its id, which should always be unique and its class, of which there can be more than one. As the button uses the id there can be only one. Depending on how many additional buttons you need several options exist. An easy one is to simply duplicate some code parts but and attach them to different buttons using a single label, so for the user they look the same. Or place your code in server.r and wrap it into an observer like so:

observer({
input$buttonid1
input$buttonid2
input$buttonid3

....your repeat code here .....

})

The ids are the unique ids of the action buttons, each must be unique If you press any of these the code gets run.

A even more powerful approach would be to use classes and use jQuery (JavaScript). See here how to grab items based on a class or id:
http://learn.jquery.com/using-jquery-core/faq/how-do-i-select-an-item-using-class-or-id/

This is how you can relate it to shiny
http://ryouready.wordpress.com/2013/11/20/sending-data-from-client-to-server-and-back-using-shiny/

In relation to buttons you may want to use shinyBS which add some nice features to shiny based on Bootstrap:

http://spark.rstudio.com/johnharrison/shinyBS-Demo/
http://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/shinyBS/index.html

Best Herman

messages.subject: Re: eval(parse(text))) in Shiny
messages.subject_clean: eval(parse(text))) in Shiny
messages.body_plain:
If you find you need eval(parse(text)) in shiny, you are almost always
on the wrong way. The super power of eval(parse()) is rarely needed,
and should be avoided for security reasons. Here is an example of how
you can achieve your goal more elegantly without security holes:

library(shiny)
runApp(list(
  ui = fluidPage(lapply(1:10, function(i) {
    uiOutput(paste0('x', i))
  })),
  server = function(input, output) {
    lapply(1:10, function(i) {
      output[[paste0('x', i)]] = renderUI(paste('Hi, this is', i))
    })
  }
))

Regards,
Yihui

Hi,

if you want to conditionally color (or more generally format) cells in tables you may want to check out the reporters  <http://davidgohel.github.io/ReporteRs/index.html>package. The FlexTables <http://davidgohel.github.io/ReporteRs/FlexTable.html> do what you want. As the name suggests, they are quite flexible.

Although the package is intended for generating Microsoft Word and PPT files via R, the underlying HTML can be extracted quite easily.

A while back I made a small Shiny toy example demo that shows the basic principle, see here <https://groups.google.com/forum/#!searchin/shiny-discuss/reporters/shiny-discuss/ZIag8igQtrc/J9PQHi7NjD8J>.

messages.subject: renderText: print each element in passed vector on a new line??
messages.subject_clean: renderText: print each element in passed vector on a new line??
messages.body_plain:
I'm fairly new at both R and Shiny with a little more experience with R. As part of a Shiny app I'm creating, I'd like to output pairs of numbers in coordinate form (ex: "(1, 2)") with each new coordinate pair on a new line. I can successfully print the pairs of numbers but they all print on the same line. Is it possible to print each on a new line using renderText?

In server.R I have the following code:

#user input determines n for findBigy1
output$summary1 <- renderText({
    dataset <- accdat
    findBigy1(input$obs1)
    })

I sourced the R script that defines this function within my Shiny app:

findBigy1 <- function(n) {
  st <- c()
  ord_ind <- order(accdat[,2], decreasing=T)
  for (i in 1:n) {
    st[i] <- paste(c("("), accdat[ord_ind[i],1 ], c(" , "), accdat[ord_ind[i], 2], c(")\n"), sep="", collapse="")
    #st[i] <- sprintf("(%f, %f)\n", accdat[ord_ind[i], 1], accdat[ord_ind[i], 3])
  }
  st
}

For a dataset with two columns this function will order the dataset based on the second column and will create a vector that saves the coordinates for the n biggest 2nd column values. (tried it two different ways)
Testing this function apart from the Shiny app produces output of the form:
 [1] "(30 , 0.29)\n" "(120 , 0.29)\n" "(230 , 0.29)\n"
The Shiny app produces output like this:
(30 , 0.29) (120 , 0.29) (230 , 0.29)

I read something that said that renderText automatically uses cat() to transform whatever is passed to a string. So it makes sense that Shiny wouldn't show the \n, but how do I get it to put each coordinate on a new line? Should I be using something other than renderText?

When I was trying to solve this I changed my findBigy1 function to return cat(st) rather than just st. This produces the correct R output:
(30 , 0.29)
 (120 , 0.29)
 (230 , 0.29)
but then the Shiny app doesn't display any coordinates in the actual app, they are all printed in the console, which is not what I want either.

The solution is probably simple enough, but I keep running around in circles changing the function and Shiny code. Any help would be greatly appreciated!  Thanks!

Melissa

Hello all,

I have been following this topic with great interest since I have been experiencing the same issue with respect to proxying via Apache.

My colleague was able to reproduce the behaviour under nginx, so this was most likely not an Apache-specific issue.

I noticed that a new package of shiny-server-1.2.0.360-amd64.deb was posted on July 14 (the problematic release was 359) but the "Shiny Server Installation" documentation has not yet been updated to reflect this.  I went ahead and installed the package and can confirm that the websockets proxying issue appears to be corrected with this release, both in Apache and nginx.

I suggest that you get yourself a copy of this package and try for yourself.

Regards,

Chris

messages.body_plain:
Let's try this:

- Copy your .RData file (let's call it mydata.RData) into the Shiny application folder (where server.R and ui.R are located)
- On top of your server.R, use load("mydata.RData")
- Stop and start Shiny Server (just to be sure you start a fresh R process)
- Launch your application

Sorry if this is what you have already been doing. Since I haven't seen your code, I just wanted you to try this and see if this works.

There are different ways to save and load your data, which you can read about online. (Refer to Help documents on "save", "save.image", and "load")

You can also add "load("path_to_data_file")" in a .Rprofile file in the user's home directory. This file is read when a new R process starts, and loads the data specified in the command. Just remember that in Shiny Server, by default, R process is owned by "shiny" user. So the .Rprofile file needs to be in /home/shiny directory, unless you have made changes to your Shiny Server configuration.

If you are still having trouble with this, send us your application code (you can send it in a private email if you prefer).

Best,
Fereshteh

messages.subject: Shiny 0.10.1 release candidate
messages.subject_clean: Shiny 0.10.1 release candidate
messages.body_plain:
Hi everyone -

We're planning to release Shiny 0.10.1 in about a week, and we would appreciate it if you could test out the release candidate version before we send a final version to CRAN. The most prominent change is extended character support. If you've encountered problems deploying apps that contain non-ASCII characters, this version should help.

Installation requires the devtools package. To install, run:
  devtools::install_github("rstudio/shiny@v/0/10/1-rc")
After installing, restart R.

The changes in this version include:

* Added Unicode support for Windows. Shiny apps running on Windows must use the
  UTF-8 encoding for ui.R and server.R (also the optional global.R) if they
  contain non-ASCII characters. See this article for details and examples:
  http://shiny.rstudio.com/gallery/unicode-characters.html (#516)

* Added an `inline` argument to `textOutput()`, `imageOutput()`, `plotOutput()`,
  and `htmlOutput()`. When `inline = TRUE`, these outputs will be put in
  `span()` instead of the default `div()`. This occurs automatically when these
  outputs are created via the inline expressions (e.g. `r textOutput(expr)`) in
  R Markdown documents. See an R Markdown example at
  http://shiny.rstudio.com/gallery/inline-output.html (#512)

* Added support for option groups in the select/selectize inputs. When the
  `choices` argument for `selectInput()`/`selectizeInput()` is a list of
  sub-lists and any sub-list is of length greater than 1, the HTML tag
  `<optgroup>` will be used. See an example at
  http://shiny.rstudio.com/gallery/option-groups-for-selectize-input.html (#542)

* `runGitHub()` also allows the 'username/repo' syntax now, which is equivalent
  to `runGitHub('repo', 'username')`. (#427)

* `navbarPage()` now accepts a `windowTitle` parameter to set the web browser
  page title to something other than the title displayed in the navbar.

If you encounter any problems with the release candidate, please let us know by filing an issue in the issue tracker on Github, or send an email to this mailing list.

Thanks!
The Shiny team

messages.subject_clean: Configuration for running Apache and Shiny server on port 80 but using different virtual host name
messages.body_plain:
This will not work, you can not have two servers listen to same port. What you can do is:

1. Let Apache listen to Port 80 and the Shiny server to port 3838
2. Create your two virtual hosts mywebpage.domain.com <http://mywebpage.domain.com/> and myShinyApp.domain.com <http://myshinyapp.domain.com/> in Apache
3. In Apache configure a proxypass rule such that all traffic to  myShinyApp.domain.com <http://myshinyapp.domain.com/> is redirected to localhost;3838 with

ProxyPass             / http://localhost:3838

messages.subject: Re: Custom Searching in DataTable
messages.subject_clean: Custom Searching in DataTable
messages.body_plain:
The last time I checked DataTables, it still did not have a
configuration option to specify whether searching should be
case-sensitive or not. An awkward solution is to type both upper and
lower cases in the search field, e.g. if you want to search for Apple,
you may use [Aa][Pp][Pp][Ll][Ee].

I'm going to work on the latest version of DataTables (1.10) soon. If
it has added such an option, I will be happy to support it.

BTW, if you are curious about how filtering is done in shiny, you can
take a look at the function shiny:::dataTablesJSON.

Regards,
Yihui

messages.body_plain:
Hi Victor,

It's important to remember that shiny applications will (by default) run as the `shiny` user on the system. The only libraries that will be visible to the shiny user are ones that are installed globally in a system library or in the shiny user's personal library. The shell script command to install a package to the system library from CRAN is:

sudo su - -c "R -e \"install.packages('shiny', repos='http://cran.rstudio.com/')\""

You could modify this to install from GitHub using devtools using:

sudo su - -c "R -e \"library(devtools); install_github('rstudio/rmarkdown')\""

That should install not to your personal library, but to the global system library making rmarkdown visible to the shiny user in most systems.

Jeff

ui.r

messages.subject: Selectize input - updating with the current value causes invalidation
messages.subject_clean: Selectize input - updating with the current value causes invalidation
messages.body_plain:
Hey guys,
I've got a single selectize input and an observer which updates the input whenever the user selects a value.
The update should do nothing - it sends a static list of choices and uses the current selection as the new selection.

However if the user quickly selects two values in a row, the value in the input object does not match the real value.
Hence, the update actually changes the selected value, which causes the observer to invalidate itself and run again.
Again, the input value is old, the selectize is changed, and the observer is thus stuck looping itself.

df.proto <- data.frame("publisher" = c(1:1000)) #the more values, the easier to reproduce the bug; works with about 50 too

shinyServer(function(input, output, session){
  observe({
    print(paste0(">>>>> ENTERING OBSERVE input$publisher: ", paste(unlist(input$publisher), collapse = ", ")))

    updateSelectizeInput(session, "publisher", choices = df.proto$publisher, selected = input[["publisher"]])

    print(paste0("EXITING OBSERVE input$publisher: ", paste(unlist(input$publisher), collapse = ", "), "<<<<<<"))
  })

shinyUI(
  navbarPage("test",

    tabPanel("Browse",
      fixedPage(
        selectizeInput("publisher", "publisher", choices = NULL, selected = NULL, multiple = T),
        HTML("</br></br></br></br></br></br></br></br></br></br></br></br></br></br></br></br></br></br></br></br></br></br></br></br></br></br></br></br>")
      )
    )
  )
)# End shiny.

I think the issue is caused by the huge list of choices - if I declare the choices in the UI and don't send them in the update call,
the bug is gone. In my production code, there are multiple selectizes which compute their respective choices based on each other,
and hence have to send these dynamic lists of possible choices using the update function, so this fix is not viable.

I'm trying to do something like updateSelectizeInput(choices = newChoices, selection = currentSelection). A user that clicks too fast
can cause the observer that the statement is in to loop on itself, which shouldn't happen as I'm not trying to change the current selection (currentSelection is always a subset of newChoices).

messages.subject: Re: Knitr knit2pdf("report.Rnw") doesn't get \ref in Shiny
messages.subject_clean: Knitr knit2pdf("report.Rnw") doesn't get \ref in Shiny
messages.body_plain:
If you compile only one time a LaTeX file then \ref{} renders in "??". You have to compile twice, without deleting the generated auxiliary file at first compilation (because the compilation reads the file from the beginning to the end, and cannot guess what \ref{} should render if its corresponding \label{} is defined later).

Then you could firstly generate the .tex file using knit() and then compile it twice using texi2pdf().

messages.subject_clean: Knitr knit2pdf("report.Rnw") doesn't get \ref in Shiny
messages.body_plain:
Note texi2pdf() was designed exactly for this purpose: to compile .tex
with the correct number of times (to resolve all references and
citations). So in theory there is no need to call texi2pdf() twice.

The offending piece might be the extra } in fig.cap="Some text here}",
which will render \caption{Some text here}} in .tex, and that is
invalid LaTeX code.

Regards,
Yihui

messages.body_plain:
My app will take two user inputted values, run them through a function, and output the outcome of the function.  My function takes two input values, runs a monte carlo simulation on those values, and spits out some outcome.

This function works perfectly fine in R and RStudio, but when I embed the function inside my shiny app, it doesn't look like the simulation portion of my function is working.  Everytime I reload my app (or hit the actionButton) with the same input values I'm getting identical results (i should get different results due to the randomness of each simulation).

Is there something specific I need to do to ensure my simulation re-runs each time I run my app?

messages.subject_clean: server-side interaction for autocomplete/suggestion to inputs
messages.body_plain:
Hi Nellster, sorry for the delayed answer. I just realized that my gmail account was the one receiving mails from google groups...

I am not sure I fully understand your question(s) as there is many points of inquiries...

I'll try to answer what I think you are missing...

Shiny server is a separate piece from the R shiny package. The shiny server basically listen to the internet and will fire up an R session running the server.R and ui.R scripts when someone points there web browser to an app URI. So, if one wants to run his own app, no need for shiny server. If one wants to write an app that will be used by others for data mining/exploration, for example, yes, you need the server (having everyone firing up a local copy of an app does not really make sense)

Since we have 5 computational servers sharing the same file system through NFS, we have shiny server install on all of our boxes. In addition, I am managing a couple of servers running on AWS instances, so yes, there is multiple ways to host a shiny server, be it internal or fully external.

As of facility, that depends on what you mean. Installing the software takes about 5 mins, just follow the instruction on the shiny server download page. Configuration is also very trivial, you need to reed the administration manual. Not sure what type of config you have in mind, but I use two models, depending on the box. On the institute server, we have per user app service configured. Everyone can put their app on their ~/ShinyApps directory and pointing a web browser to http://shiny.institute.org/myId/myApp will fire up a given user app. On the aws boxes, I am using a single directory and the shiny user is the own who own the processes.

That said, the management of a computational/web server is a different storry. Difficulty will depends on your ease with admistarting a unix box and your understanding of network communication in general. Not sure exactly how one could start, but testing stuff on an AWS instance first (or a VM if you guys run unix machines as VMs) makes it for a less painful learning curve.

I'll post some notes and links to the documents once I'm in front of a computer (I'm on an iPad right now)

Let me know if you have other questions

Marco

messages.subject: Shiny: Reverse Proxy and websockets problem
messages.subject_clean: Shiny: Reverse Proxy and websockets problem
messages.body_plain:
I'm developing an app (http://urbanstreams.net/tools/bugmodels/) which was working fine until I put it under a reverse proxy (Shiny-server 0.4.0.15, using Apache2 2.4.7, Ubuntu 14.04 - as per the instructions for Rstudio/shiny).

When the app is loaded under a reverse proxy, Firefox's JS inspector returns

"GET http://urbanstreams.net/tools/bugmodels/__sockjs__/017/jdq4jk8b/websocket [HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request 32ms]
Firefox can't establish a connection to the server at ws://urbanstreams.net/tools/bugmodels/__sockjs__/017/jdq4jk8b/websocket <http://urbanstreams.net/tools/bugmodels/__sockjs__/017/jdq4jk8b/websocket>. [sockjs-0.3.min.js:27]"

The app continues to function ok (after selecting a stream and a site on the first tab, all of the controls on all of the tabs work fine), until you return to the first tab and attempt to select another stream.  At that point, the app grays out with the following message on the JS inspector.
"POST http://urbanstreams.net/tools/bugmodels/__sockjs__/017/f5ur9uwf/xhr_send [HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden 13ms]"

I see that others have had trouble with websockets and shiny with a reverse proxy (mostly from a year ago), but I haven't been able to find any reports of this problem.

Thanks!

Thanks for any help you can provide.

Hi all,

I'm having an issue with the updateSelectizeInput function when I include the argument "server = TRUE". It looks like that when I type in something in the box, it does not find any match with the choice that are available.

Here is an example of the code to reproduce the problem (I copied the session info at the end of the message):

# ui.R
library (shiny)
shinyUI(
  fluidPage(
    sidebarLayout(
      sidebarPanel(
        selectizeInput("gene", h4("Gene"), choices = c("Enter gene, eg: EGFR" = ""))
      ),
      mainPanel(
        verbatimTextOutput('text')
      )
    )
  )
)

# server.R
gene_names <- c("a","b","c","d","e","f","g")

shinyServer(function(input, output, session) {
    updateSelectizeInput(session, "gene",  choices = gene_names, server = TRUE)
    output$text <- renderText({ paste("gene", input$gene)
    })
})

Any help would be greatly appreciated!!
Best,
Massimo

ggvisOutput %>% column %>% fluidRow %>% tabsetPanel %>% navbarPage

Ian

Hi Everyone,

I have some problem with the reactivity of shiny.

I have a (global) data frame called table.of.peaks which the app displays trough peakTable() function. When the 'Add' button is pressed, the app adds a new row to the table (the data of the row is collected from the UI input fields "separated" by using isolate() function).

The sequence of function calling is the following (starting from the function where the input$add.button takes place):
readPeak() - the data from the UI is collected and sent (as a one row data frame, let's call it Row) to the function from where the readPeak() have been called (makeTable())
makeTable() - the Row here is added to the global table.of.peaks table, and the function return with this global data frame
peakTable() - the global table.of.peaks variable (return value of makeTable() function) is displayed
During operation, always the actual value of the table can be seen, and when the Add button is pressed, the table is updated and printed out again.

My question is, can i add a Delete button to the app that works the same way as the Add button (get the row index we want to delete from the UI) without using Javascript or other "external" solutions? The app would work the same, but table would be updated from a func. called for example delPeak() if the Delete button is pressed. So the sequence would look like delPeak() -> makeTable() -> peakTable(), and if Add button is pressed the sequence would be the same as above.

I didn't include any source code, because there aren't any errors yet, i'm just planning the implementation, and searching for a simple method.

Thanks for the help in advance.

Hi,

How may I detect/determine which browser the client is using from within Shiny?

Our corporate standard is IE8. I'd like my app to detect the browser type and display a message to switch to chrome or firefox if the browser is IE. This is a very high source of frustration right now. I send folks a link to an app. I forget to remind them to use Chrome. Even if I remember, they still just click on the link. And even for regular users, it doesn't work out well for them to switch their default browser. All of our enterprise apps are requiring IE8. So if a user switches they get frustrated because in their job they use the enterprise stuff more than the shiny app I'm working on.

Too bad folks can't just right click on the link and select "open with" like they can on files in windows explorer. Or it would be cludgy but cool if there was a browser proxy type app that you could install and set as default browser. Such that when you click on a link, that app would run, and list all browsers installed on the computer, and let the user pick which one to run. I would love it myself. Anyone know of such an app out there?

Jonathan

Andrew, I have a similar issue with reactiveFileReader, and I hope it's ok if I post it here, so perhaps people that replied to you before will see this as well. Besides, you could see how it can be used more or less successfully.

Here's my code for server.R file for a Shiny app, notice that hours is now a function that you will refer to as hours() further.

#server.R
require(rCharts)
shinyServer(
  function(input, output, session) {
       hours <- reactiveFileReader(1000, session, 'data/hours.csv', read.csv)
          output$chart1 <- renderChart({
          HoursPlot <- hPlot(x="Manager", y="HoursLogged", type="bar", data=hours(), title = "Hours Logged This Month")
          HoursPlot$yAxis(title = list(text = "Hours Logged"))
          HoursPlot$addParams(height = 600, dom = 'chart1')
          return(HoursPlot)
          })

  }
)

According to the manual of reactiveFileReader this placement of the function inside shinyServer() will make it work per-session, and it actually works great inside RStudio (I have Windows): every time I make changes to the hours.csv file in data folder, it instantly updates the chart in RStudio. However, once deployed on Shinyapps.io it only shows static data (what was originally in hours.csv), it doesn't seem to update reactively as it should. I know if I re-deploy the app, the data will be refreshed, but what's the point of reactiveFileReader() then? I would really like for it to work properly, and if I place this function outside of shinyServer() (above the call), it will load for a second and shut down, which is not acceptable obviously.

Please advise. Thank you!

messages.body_plain:
Hi Saurabh,

Here's a solution to your issue (at least it worked for me). For ui.R make sure to have a "selected" argument, so there's a default. For server.R, wrap your paste0() inside a "reactive({})" function

#ui.R

library(shiny)

shinyUI(fluidPage(

  # Application title
  titlePanel("Mydata"),

  # Sidebar with a slider input for number of bins
  sidebarLayout(
    sidebarPanel(

      selectInput(inputId = "folder", label = "Select the folder to get the data", choices = c("A", "B", "C"), selected = "A")

    ),

    # Show a plot of the generated distribution
    mainPanel(

      tableOutput(outputId = "dataDisplay")
    )
  )
))

#server.R
library(shiny)

shinyServer(function(input, output, session) {
  file <- reactive({paste0(input$folder, "/data.csv")})
  data <- reactiveFileReader(intervalMillis = 1000, session, filePath = file, readFunc = read.csv)

 output$dataDisplay <- renderTable({
   data()

  })

})

Let me know you have any questions.

This does look like an issue with how ggvis interacts with sub-applications in Shiny. Could you file an issue with ggvis?

-Winston

On Tue, Jul 29, 2014 at 9:24 AM, Ian Lyttle <ijly...@me.com> wrote:

> Hi Everyone,
>
> I think I might have a some potential issues to file, but I'd like some guidance from the RStudio folks on how best to proceed. File issues? For which package(s)?
>
> Of course, it is a strong possibility that I am just "doing it wrong".
>
> There are two issues, both of which appear in this composition:
>
> ggvisOutput %>% column %>% fluidRow %>% tabsetPanel %>% navbarPage
>
> One appears only when rmarkdown is rendered, the other only when run from the command-line.
>
> (1) Rendered rmarkdown: This may be related to the app/subApp structure I understand to be used in shiny (https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/issues/548). Only the ggvis that is part of the default tabsetPanel renders close to correctly.
>
> (2) Shiny from the command line (using my example: > app_test), both graphs render legibly, but in contrast to (1), the ggvis are not respecting the horizontal size of the column.
>
> Despite efforts to make the code minimal, it's a bit bulky, so I made a gist, including sessionInfo().
>
> https://gist.github.com/ijlyttle/a37bea7952f1ac9f12ba
>
> Thanks, as always, for putting up with all of my feedback,
>
> Ian
>

messages.subject: Re: getting utf8 to display
messages.subject_clean: getting utf8 to display
messages.body_plain:
No, do not use options(encoding = 'UTF-8') in global.R or anywhere. It
is a bad thing to do, which makes the assumption that everything is
UTF-8 encoded in your R session, and this is often not true.

Regards,
Yihui

On Thu, Jul 31, 2014 at 12:49 AM, 'ignorant' via Shiny - Web Framework
for R <shiny-...@googlegroups.com> wrote:
> Hi there,
>
> I am trying the new version that is supposed to take care of utf-8 issues
> but I am not able to get it working. For example, the following text does
> not display for me -
>
> verbatimTextOutput("summary这里也可以用中文"),
>
> (above copied from example -
> http://shiny.rstudio.com/gallery/unicode-characters.html
> I am using the dev version of shiny. file ui.R confirms that this file is
> now UTF-8.
>
> My OS is Ubuntu 4.8.2-19 with the following variable set -
> LANG=en_US.UTF-8
>
> My R session is -
>> sessionInfo()
> R version 3.1.1 (2014-07-10)
> Platform: x86_64-pc-linux-gnu (64-bit)
>
> locale:
>  [1] LC_CTYPE=en_US.UTF-8       LC_NUMERIC=C
>  [3] LC_TIME=en_US.UTF-8        LC_COLLATE=en_US.UTF-8
>  [5] LC_MONETARY=en_US.UTF-8    LC_MESSAGES=en_US.UTF-8
>  [7] LC_PAPER=en_US.UTF-8       LC_NAME=C
>  [9] LC_ADDRESS=C               LC_TELEPHONE=C
> [11] LC_MEASUREMENT=en_US.UTF-8 LC_IDENTIFICATION=C
>
> I have the following in my global.R (not sure if necessary) -
> options(shiny.usecairo = FALSE)
> options(encoding = 'UTF-8')
>
>
> Any help would be appreciated.
messages.body_snippet:
No, do not use options(encoding = 'UTF-8') in global.R or anywhere. It
is a bad thing to do, which makes the assumption that everything is
UTF-8 encoded in your R session, and this is often not true.
